[JIMB0] @brenwildman begs to differ. Apparently some resistive heaters have discovered a way around the first law of thermodynamics.
[brenwildman] @JIMB0: Huh? ~1:1 is correct, 1:1 is technically incorrect. Some heaters are lower due to poor power factor (from the inductive fan) and due to converting the energy into unwanted forms that can be lost from the system (eg. sound). These effects are minor but real and measurable. There is no violation of the first law here nor does all energy need to be converted to heat to satisfy the first law as you incorrectly claim.

[Furi8] The maximum power for a standard 240V outlet in Australia is 2400 watts, based on a maximum current of 10 amps (P = VI, so 240V x 10A = 2400W).

[JimB] From AI - Water freezes at 32°F (0°C), but household pipes typically do not freeze until outdoor temperatures drop to 20°F (-7°C) or lower
If you're at risk of water pipes freezing in Australia, your little fan Kmart Convection LED Heater ain't going to do much lol.
[banana365] That's where AI has failed you again. My parent's place in the UK is often left empty for a week or so. Years ago it used to have burst pipes every so often, then they put a small, cheap heater in that they left running on a low setting. The place would still be really cold when returning during bad winters, but just that few degrees above zero was perfectly adequate to stop pipes freezing.

It has a full and half power modes (which I use the most) so it can limit the power use some what.
